subject: Post-call: Skyline payments discovery — cost anchors & pilot ROI
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@skylpay.com>, salesops@skylpay.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Skyline payments discovery — cost anchors & pilot ROI

Hi Sarah / Skyline team,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- High per-transaction latency causing drop-offs in fraud challenge flow (peak windows ~18:00-20:00 PT).
- Current vendor costs are spiking with token growth; finance wants a predictable unit cost to model 2028 budgeting.
- Concern about data isolation / audit trail for playback and disputes.

Goals we heard
- Proof-of-value pilot that demonstrates >=40% per-token cost reduction on your fraud pipeline OR latency improvement to <120ms median at peak.
- A 6–8 week pilot that includes realistic traffic shaping (spike windows), instrumentation for token-level billing, and an ops runbook for failover.

Initial token economics / levers we discussed
- Model choice + quantization: narrow model family selection for fraud scoring; estimate ~2.8x cost delta between full FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants for your average request.
- Batching & continuous KV cache: prefix caching for re-used contexts (merchant metadata) and small batch windows during peak to improve throughput without hurting tail latency. Preliminary ballpark: 25–35% TCO upside from caching + batching for this workload.
- Fallback routing: hybrid routing to cheaper variants on non-critical requests to shave incremental spend.

Open constraints you called out
- Budget: procurement looking at a $60–80k first-half pilot commitment (total spend cap).
- Security: need SOC 2 in place and ability to route logs to your SIEM; will need an NDA + any attestation.

Proposed next steps (what I can do and by when)
1) Share a short pilot scope + token-econ worksheet (attached) with sample TCO scenarios — EOD tomorrow.
2) Align on traffic profile and sample payloads (you to share anonymized examples) — target by next Tue 7/6.
3) Draft a lightweight SOW for a 6-week pilot w/ success criteria and cost cap — I’ll have a draft by 7/8.

Ask from you
- Confirm pilot budget cap ($60k–$80k) and decision owners for procurement + security so I can tailor the SOW.
- Share a small set of representative payloads (10–20) and a 24-hr spike window sample.

Attachments: skyline-pilot-scope.pdf (pilot scope), token-econ-workbook.xlsx (TCO scenarios)

Thanks — will follow up with the workbook tonight.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@skylpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: salesops@skylpay.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Skyline payments discovery — cost anchors & pilot ROI

Thanks Marcus — this looks right, appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget: Procurement signed off on a hard cap of $70k for the pilot. They want the SOW to include a spend kill-switch if we hit 90% of that cap.
2) Success criteria: In addition to cost/latency, we need an objective on false-positive rate change — engineering would like to ensure score drift is <1% compared to production baseline.
3) Data: We can share anonymized payloads and a 48-hour log sample (will send by Monday).

A couple operational asks:
- We need attestations for SOC 2 Type II or equivalent and a simple diagram of where logs land.
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-request redaction for PCI-sensitive fields before logs are stored?

We look forward to the workbook. Once we have the SOW draft, I’ll route to procurement with the $70k cap and the kill-switch requirement.

—Sarah
Sarah O'Neill
Head of Payments Product | Skyline Payments
sarah.oneill@skylpay.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Skyline payments discovery — cost anchors & pilot ROI

Looping in CS and Solutions to capture operational checklist and start a scoped SOW. Notes/actions from my side:

- I’ll own the SOC 2 attestation/package and the logging diagram. Expected drop-in: standard SOC 2 pack + supplemental logs export instructions (ETA 7/7).
- Solutions will run a quick heatmap of expected token distribution vs. payloads you share and return a baseline TCO scenario by 7/2.
- For per-request redaction: yes — Redwood supports configurable redaction rules at ingestion and we can apply PCI field redaction before persistence. I’ll include the config snippet in the SOW appendix.

Immediate asks from us to Skyline:
- Procurement contact name + email (so we can include the kill-switch language formally).
- Sample payloads + 48-hr log sample (anonymized) — please deliver to the Drive link below.

I’ll attach an initial SOW template to the Drive folder and drop the SOC 2 stub there. Marcus — can you push the token-econ workbook now so I can start the scenario work?
